messages.content: Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

# Dark mode, at last

Dark mode arrives today in Margin 3.4, on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android. Turn it on in Settings → Appearance, or leave it on Auto and it tracks your system clock.

The requests started in 2023. It seems fair to explain the delay.

We had a version running a year ago. Flip the palette, ship it, done. It read badly. Notes are mostly small text, and white on black smears at 14px; the letterforms bleed into each other, worst of all on OLED. What we shipped instead is #E8E6E3 on #1A1A1A, which measures 13.2:1 and kills the halo.

Then there was the highlighter. All five colors were chosen against a white page, and against a dark one the yellow glowed like a traffic sign. Every color is retuned, and existing highlights convert as the file opens, so a note you marked up in 2024 still looks like what you intended.

Two other details. Images and PDFs keep their full brightness rather than getting dimmed, since a dimmed screenshot is a screenshot nobody can read. And code blocks get a purpose-built syntax theme instead of the light one with its colors swapped.

If anything looks off, whether it's a plugin with hardcoded colors or a theme that fights the new tokens, mail support@margin.app with a screenshot. Someone is reading that inbox all week.

Update through the App Store, the Play Store, or Help → Check for Updates.

*(No real app name was supplied, so "Margin" and margin.app are left in place for you to swap.)*

# Dark mode is here

Margin 3.4 brings dark mode to Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android as of today. Switch it on under Settings → Appearance, or set it to Auto and let it follow your system clock.

People have been asking since 2023, so the delay deserves a word.

A build existed twelve months ago. Invert the palette and ship. It read terribly. Notes are mostly small text, and white on black smudges at 14px; letterforms run together, and OLED screens make it worse. The version you're getting uses #E8E6E3 on #1A1A1A, a 13.2:1 ratio with no halo around the type.

The highlighter was its own problem. All five colors were picked to sit on a white page, and on a dark one the yellow burned like a road sign. Each color has been retuned, and old highlights convert when the file opens, so a note you marked up in 2024 reads the way you meant it to.

Two smaller things. Images and PDFs stay at full brightness instead of being dimmed, because a dimmed screenshot is unreadable. And code blocks use a syntax theme built for dark backgrounds rather than the light one with inverted colors.

Something looking wrong? A plugin with hardcoded colors, a theme arguing with the new tokens? Send a screenshot to support@margin.app. The inbox is staffed all week.

Grab the update from the App Store, the Play Store, or Help → Check for Updates.
